speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-year-old having trouble sleeping because you wake up frightened. Can you tell me if you have any nightmares, if you snore, or if anyone else in your home has similar sleep issues?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual. with perspicacious discernment

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Night Terrors. The symptoms of sudden awakening with screaming, no confusion afterward, and residual fatigue are classic for sleep terrors in children, distinguishing them from nightmares.
